title: Grime
label: Rephlex
format: Compilation: CD (Village Voice) and vinyl ('triple-pack LP' per Plastician; k-punk calls it an LP)

type.basis: An early use of the word grime as a release title, on an established electronic label: evidence for when and how the name was fixed.

sound.text: k-punk: no MCs; a South London grime with the 'silver impersonality and sleekness of stainless steel'.
Mark One's 'Stargate 92': menacing beats with early-1990s synths and MC grunts; 'Raindance' sets repeated female vocal samples over dark, repetitive bass.
The Village Voice hears the album's dread carried by the '18 wheels of Plasticman's Industrial Graft'.
Slaughter Mob: Jamaican-accented vocals and deep, rolling bass on 'Dub Weapon'; door creaks and owl hoots on 'Creeky Door'.

context.text: Plastician said in 2004 that Rephlex's Grant Wilson-Claridge saw him play FWD>> at Plastic People and asked for beats; in 2017 he called it 'the first grime CD'.
Rephlex used the line 'Grime. Sublow. Dubstep... It's Music' in 2004 (as quoted by a record shop).
Plastician himself said it 'was kind of grime, but it wasn't specifically'.
A Vice 'Beats' columnist questioned whether Rephlex understood grime, given the tracklisting.
Followed by 'Grime 2' (CAT 160), which Plastician said was technically dubstep.

rels.other: Technotronic – 'Pump Up the Jam' (Plasticman's track reworks it, per k-punk)

uncertainty: Wikipedia gives the catalogue number CAT 156 but no date. The track titles differ between reviews ('Camel Aide'/'Camel Ride'), and k-punk's 'Pump up the Jam' may be the 'Pump' named in the brief. The Vice 'Beats' column remark comes from https://www.vice.com/en/article/beats-v11n4/. This is a compilation and arguably closer to proto-dubstep; register it as a crossover document.
tracklist: About four tracks per artist. Named tracks: Mark One 'Stargate 92', 'Raindance', 'Interference'; Plasticman 'Pump up the Jam' (k-punk) / 'Camel Ride' or 'Camel Aide' / 'Industrial Graft' / 'The Music'; Slaughter Mob 'Dub Weapon', 'Creeky Door'. Titles differ slightly between reviews.
